newsitem.title: USA: LDC DEBT TURNS MIXED LATE, AWAITS U.S. DATA ON WED.
newsitem.headline: LDC DEBT TURNS MIXED LATE, AWAITS U.S. DATA ON WED.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices turned mixed in light trading Tuesday as investors got ready for imminent U.S. economic reports, traders and analysts said.
Late selling in synch with U.S. Treasuries reversed earlier gains brought about by short-covering, they said.
Investors held their defensive stance ahead of the U.S. retail sales and producer price data set for release on Wednesday.
"My impression is that things are very quiet and we've got very narrow movement," said Dan Peirce, chief emerging markets strategist at Bank of Boston.
Among major Latin Brady debt, Brazil "C" bonds were off 1/4 at 82-3/4, mainly in tandem with Treasuries, traders said.

On Monday evening, Brazil reported its trade deficit jumped in July because of a surge in capital goods imports rather than a last-minute spurt of oil imports, as many economists thought. The announcement affected prices little, but reinforced the sentiment the deficit surge could be blamed on special factors.
Elsewhwere, Argentina FRBs were up 1/4 at 95-3/4 and Mexico Pars off 1/4 at 79-3/4.
Russian debt continued its recent kick, with dollar- denominated Vnesh loans quoted up one point at 102-1/8.
"We still see buyers in New York for Vnesh and Prins," one trader said.
On Wednesday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, the market eyes long- awaited reports on the July performance of U.S. retail sales and the Producer Price Index.
Wall Street economists forecast retail sales up 0.7 percent and PPI up 0.1 percent.
The emerging debt market appears well-positioned for the data and could see a relief rally if the figures come in near consensus, Bank of Boston's Peirce said.
"The market might be vulnerable to a weaker-than-expected number, given the fact that people have built in a lot of ugly expectations and fears over the last week or so," he said.
